text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Doctors, nurses and social workers, whose strike will enter sixth week on Monday, demand resignation of the government.
- Yugoslavia and Croatia agreed on a draft social insurance accord.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno partner, the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO), blocks verification of Zajedno mandates in the federal parliament.
- Nineteen Serb families from Kosovo are striking for the eighth day in Belgrade demanding solution to their housing problem.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic is opposed to proposed changes to the federal constitution.
- Serbia's PKB Banka said it would sue the central bank for an unconstitutional decision to close it over insolvency.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia's Supreme Defence Council said the Yugoslav border is completely secure.
- Yugoslavia and Poland signed agreements on avoidance of double taxation, cooperation in medicine and agriculture during the visit of Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to Warsaw.
- Kosovo is a part of Serbia and will remain so, said Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic and called on Kosovo Albanians to take part in Yugoslavia's political institutions.
- Transition of Yugoslav economy will be impossible without international financial aid, participants of the Yugoslav economists' congress in Petrovac said.
- Proposed changes of the federal constitution will not hurt the equality of the two federal units, spokesman of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia Ivica Dacic said.
- Privatisation in Montenegro is in a critical stage and is at the moment spurring a lot of discontent, Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic told an economists' congress.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Businessman and owner of BK TV Bogoljub Karic has decided not to run for Serbian presidential elections.
BLIC
- Some 800 Serbian firms are not paying their health fund contributions.
POLITIKA EKSPRES

- Good economic programmes will secure sources for financing and modernising the Yugoslav army and ensure better standard for its members, says Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic on tour of Yugoslav army units in Belgrade.
- Draft law on ownership transformation prevents cheap sell-off and under-estimation of the value of state and socially owned property, says Socialist Party of Serbia vice-president Milorad Vucelic.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- Montgenegrin President Momir Bulatovic said he would back Slobodan Milosevic's nomination for federal president.
- The government asks resignation of TV Montenegro editor-in-chief Vladimir Asanin because he violated information and constitution laws.
- Summer Festival of the Budva city theatre will open on July 1.
MONITOR

- President Bulatovic organised a secret meeting of his supporters in Bar in order to secure a presidential nomination but the rival faction of Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic discovered the plan and thwarted it.
- There are 28,300 refugees in Montenegro, of whom 70 percent are from Bosnia. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
